messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but likely they want the standard error or maybe the p-value? They provide sample mean 98.2, std dev 1.4, sample size 40, population mean 98.6. They ask to calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. That might refer to the standard error of the mean under null: sigma/sqrt(n). But we don't know population sigma; we have sample std dev 1.4. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.221. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null: same as standard error. So answer: about 0.221.

But maybe they want to compute the p-value using the function. The function calculates p-value given sample mean, population mean, sample std dev, sample size, two_tailed. We can call it. Let's do that.
